newsitem.title: USA: Most U.S. spot resids steady despite colder temps.
newsitem.headline: Most U.S. spot resids steady despite colder temps.

text.p: U.S. spot fuel oil prices mostly held steady Friday despite forecasts for colder East Coast weather, with sentiment still weighed down by ample inventories and sluggish utility interest, sources said.
"The market's been watching the weather, but we still need to see some utility burns," said one cash trader, adding some protracted cold was needed to trim stocks.

In New York Harbor, physical one percent was unchanged at about $19 a barrel. Traders said January paper was off slightly with crude to $18.65-85, while February paper was quoted steady in the high-$18 area.
NYH prompt 0.3 percent high pour notionally was little changed at $20.75-21.00 but offers later in the month closer to $20.25 led to expectations of softer numbers ahead.
High sulphurs in New York again held steady.
At the U.S. Gulf, one percent eased slightly to about $18, while three percent slipped more than 50 cents to below $16.
No NYH or USG deals were reported.

New York city gate weekend gas prices climbed almost 50 cents Friday to the $4.50/mmBtu area on prospects for colder East Coast temperatures. NYH one percent resid was still at a $3.01/mmBtu equivalent.
